answer: Persistent attention ledger. Each agent identity accrues a slow-decaying activity score; to keep access it must continuously answer unpredictable micro-challenges whose difficulty tracks background nebula-level noise in the network. Above a ridge threshold of concurrent identities per operator, challenge frequency scales so a farm must spend real compute-hours per identity per day. The mechanism costs an attacker that sustained compute and interrupt latency, since a dormancy gaps decay the signal below the access floor.
